classification.difficultyReason: Account for the path width on both sides of each garden dimension, subtract the garden area, reconcile square metres with square centimetres, and divide by the right-triangular paver area.

inlines.text: A path 1.8 m wide is being built around a rectangular garden.
The garden is 8.4 m long and 5.4 m wide. The path is shaded in the diagram.
The path is to be covered with triangular pavers with side lengths of 15 cm and 20 cm as shown. How many pavers are needed?

spec.description: A rectangular garden inside an outer rectangle, with restrained diagonal hatching identifying the surrounding path. Preserve all four dimension arrows, the Garden label and NOT TO SCALE.
spec.mathematics: The inner rectangle measures 8.4 m by 5.4 m. The path is 1.8 m wide on every side. Dimension arrows above and right of the inner rectangle measure the garden; arrows across the left and bottom strips measure path width.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and region labels are visible; outer dimensions and calculated areas are absent.

spec.description: One right triangular paver, with a vertical left side, horizontal bottom side and hypotenuse descending to the right. Preserve the right-angle marker, One paver heading and NOT TO SCALE.
spec.mathematics: The perpendicular sides are 15 cm and 20 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied lengths and right-angle marker are visible.

answer.worked:
The path adds $1.8\ \text{m}$ on each side of the garden.
$$\begin{align*}
L_{\text{outer}} &= 8.4+2\times1.8=12\ \text{m} \\
W_{\text{outer}} &= 5.4+2\times1.8=9\ \text{m} \\
A_{\text{path}} &= 12\times9-8.4\times5.4 \\
A_{\text{path}} &= 62.64\ \text{m}^{2} \\
A_{\text{path}} &= 626400\ \text{cm}^{2} \\
A_{\text{paver}} &= \frac12\times20\times15 \\
A_{\text{paver}} &= 150\ \text{cm}^{2} \\
N_{\text{pavers}} &= \frac{626400}{150} \\
N_{\text{pavers}} &= 4176
\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $4176$ pavers are needed.
